slides.title: Non-Virtual Destructor Bug
slides.prompt: What happens if you execute 'delete basePtr' where basePtr points to a Derived object, but Base destructor is NOT virtual?
options: Undefined behavior (only Base destructor runs, causing memory leak of Derived resources)
Both Base and Derived destructors run safely
Derived destructor runs, but Base destructor is skipped
slides.correctAnswer: Undefined behavior (only Base destructor runs, causing memory leak of Derived resources)

slides.title: When to Omit Virtual Destructor
slides.prompt: When is it safe to omit a virtual destructor in a class?
options: When the class is not intended to be used as a polymorphic base class
When the class contains private member variables
When the class inherits from std::string
slides.correctAnswer: When the class is not intended to be used as a polymorphic base class

slides.title: Smart Pointer Polymorphic Deletion
slides.prompt: How does 'std::shared_ptr<Base> sp = std::make_shared<Derived>();' handle deletion if ~Base() is non-virtual?
options: shared_ptr captures the correct Derived deleter at construction, avoiding memory leak
Leaks the Derived class portion completely
slides.correctAnswer: shared_ptr captures the correct Derived deleter at construction, avoiding memory leak

slides.title: Virtual Constructing Idiom
slides.prompt: Since constructors cannot be virtual in C++, how is 'virtual object cloning' implemented?
options: By defining a custom virtual clone() method returning a copy of derived object
By calling new operator inside destructor
By type casting vtable pointer manually
slides.correctAnswer: By defining a custom virtual clone() method returning a copy of derived object
